title: Act III — A More Perfect Union (1782–1789)

missions.title: The Idle Camp
missions.location: New Windsor Cantonment, Newburgh, New York
missions.summary: Peace rumored, pay years in arrears, the officers furious at Congress. The hub systems turn dark: keep discipline in an army with nothing left to fight and every reason to march on Philadelphia. The quietest and most dangerous winter of the war.

objectives.text: Hold desertion and dueling in check through the idle months
The anonymous addresses circulate — learn who in YOUR mess is listening

missions.title: The Newburgh Address
missions.location: The Temple of Virtue, New Windsor Cantonment
missions.summary: The near-coup, played as an influence scene among officers you have served with for eight years. You choose where you stand BEFORE Washington unexpectedly enters — the game remembers your answer even though history supplies the outcome. He reads his address to cold silence; then, fumbling with a letter, puts on his spectacles: 'I have not only grown gray but almost blind in the service of my country.' The room breaks. The republic survives its most dangerous hour.

objectives.text: Before the meeting: your voice in the mess — for the memorial, for patience, or silence
The assembly: witness (interactive staging, documented beats)

missions.title: Evacuation Day
missions.summary: March into liberated New York behind Knox as the last British boats pull for the fleet. At the Battery the flagstaff is greased and the ensign nailed up — a sailor named Van Arsdale climbs it with cleats as the crowd roars: the act's one moment of pure joy. In the harbor's background, the codex notes the other exodus: Black Loyalists sailing to Nova Scotia under the Book of Negroes, free by British ledger and lost to the new republic.

objectives.text: The procession: your brigade's place of honor down the Bowery
Field Journal: the Book of Negroes and the 60,000 who left

missions.title: Farewell
missions.location: Fraunces Tavern, New York — then the Maryland State House, Annapolis
missions.summary: Two rooms, one lesson. Fraunces Tavern: Washington, unable to speak, embraces each officer in silence — Knox first. Annapolis, December 23: hands trembling, he returns his commission to the civilian Congress — 'Having now finished the work assigned me, I retire from the great theatre of Action' — and rides for home to keep Christmas. The scene that made the republic real.

missions.title: Home
missions.summary: Demobilized without back pay; your land certificates trade at pennies on the dollar to speculators. Plant, mend, bury, remember. A quiet, Joseph Plumb Martin-toned chapter — 'we were turned adrift like old worn-out horses' — that plants the seeds of everything that follows.

objectives.text: A season at home: the farm, the debts, the neighbors who stayed
Sell your certificates now, or hold paper that may never pay (the game does not tell you Hamilton is coming)

missions.title: Brothers' Blood
missions.summary: Shays' Rebellion. Farmers ruined by debt and taxes — many of them your own veterans; the roster system makes this literal — march on the armory behind Daniel Shays, a Bunker Hill veteran wearing the sword he was given for it. Shepard's militia fires warning shots, then grapeshot over open snow: four dead, no musket volley ever exchanged. The game's hardest scene because the enemy is your own muster roll, and the fight barely happens.

objectives.text: Which side of the field are you on? Both are staffed with names you know
The standoff: hold or advance — either way, live with the four in the snow
Field Journal: the debt chain from unpaid soldier to Springfield, and what it did to the Articles' reputation

missions.title: The Room Where the Union Was Argued
missions.location: taverns and print shops around the State House, Philadelphia
missions.summary: You are not inside the Convention — the windows are nailed shut and the delegates sworn to silence — but a veteran officer's word carries weight in the City Tavern, and Springfield is the argument on every table. Debate vignette; the codex carries the Federalist and Anti-Federalist cases in their own words.

objectives.text: Three conversations: a Shaysite exile, a nationalist officer of your old line, a printer setting both sides in type
Field Journal: Brutus and Publius, fairly matched

missions.title: The First Citizen
missions.location: Federal Hall, Wall Street, New York
missions.summary: The inauguration on the Federal Hall balcony — the oath, the roar, 'Long live George Washington.' The camera finds your character in the crowd, older, and as the bells ring the game opens the memorial book: every soldier you lost, 1775 to 1787, name by name, as the closing credits. The republic they bought is the player's to weigh.
